data.name: Flint
data.gender_notes: Flint is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English word ‘fleotan’ meaning ‘to strike’ or ‘stone’. Flint was used as a weapon material and for making fire. In the Bible, it is mentioned in Genesis as the material used for the first altar by Abraham. The name Flint carries the meaning “Stone, strong, enduring” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Flint usually hope their child will grow to embody stone, strong, enduring and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Flint belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Stone, strong, enduring.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Flint total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Flint" has a strong historical associated with craftsmanship, specifically with regards to the production of tools and weapons. Its etymology relating to the Old English word 'fleotan' conjures images of strength, resilience, and the ability to survive through adversity. This name is symbolic of one who is resourceful, determined, and capable of making things happen in the face of challenges.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name "Flint" carries an element of fire and passion. The biblical connection with the use of flint in building the first altar by Abraham is reminder of our call to offer ourselves as a living sacrifice to God. Just as the flint is struck to produce a spark that ignites a fire, so too are we called to light a fire within ourselves and others through our actions, faith, and love. This name can inspire a deep sense of commitment, dedication, and a powerful connection to the divine.
